examples.explanation: The examples demonstrate unchanged acyl-group names used as substituent prefixes.
The source examples instantiate the class-word, multiplicative-prefix, and retained-prefix rules.
The examples demonstrate pseudohalide class naming and seniority.
These names are formed from carbonyl, carbamoyl, and related acyl-group names.
The acid name precedes the halide or pseudohalide class names because no acyl-group name exists.
The preferred names use method 1; cyanic chloride and cyanic azide illustrate method 2.
The examples compare the three substituent-expression methods and their preferred uses.
The examples cover retained names, multiplicative cations, and alphabetical ordering of unlike cations.
The cyclic salt is named as a heterocycle.
The examples contrast substitutive method 1 with hydrogen-anion method 2.
Preferred names for organic derivatives of inorganic oxoacids use method 2.
The example records the distinct inorganic-chemistry orthographic convention.
The examples satisfy the pseudoester definition and rank as esters.

value.condition: all suffix-expressed acid hydroxy groups are replaced by F, Cl, Br, or I
construction: derive the acyl-group name under P-65.1.7
append each specific halide class as a separate word

value.condition: all suffix-expressed acid hydroxy groups are replaced by N3, CN, NC, NCO, NCS, NCSe, or NCTe
construction: derive the acyl-group name under P-65.1.7
append each pseudohalide class as a separate word

semantic_units.term: retained acyl names permitted in preferred acyl pseudohalide names

value.construction: use the corresponding acyl-group name to form the acyl-halide name

value.condition: no acyl-group name exists for the di- or polycarbonic acid
value.construction: cite the acid name followed by the halide class name or names

methods.1: name as an acyl halide or pseudohalide of carbononitridic acid
methods.2: cite the halide or pseudohalide name after cyanic acid

methods.1: prefix derived from the acid name, such as carbonochloridoyl
methods.2: compound prefix: halo or halogeno prefix plus an appropriate divalent acyl group, such as fluorosulfonyl
methods.3: at an acyclic-chain end use a halide or pseudohalide prefix plus oxo or its chalcogen analogue

value.trigger: another group is principal or the acyl group is attached to another substituent

value.salt_prefix: cation name as a separate preceding word

value.construction: cite cation name or names, then the anion name as a separate word
value.retained_names: all retained acid names may be used without restriction

value.construction: name the cyclic salt as a heterocycle

anionic_prefixes.chalcogen_analogues: form corresponding selenium and tellurium prefixes analogously

method_1.construction: cite the free acid as a prefix to the anion name

method_2.construction: insert hydrogen, with di-, tri-, etc. as required, between cation names and the anion name

value.rule: write hydrogen directly before the anion name without a space when it is part of the anion

value.extended_description: acyl derivative of an alcohol or corresponding chalcogen analogue
